title: Eleven Witnesses and One Bench
subtitle: 法律规则 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）
meta: 主题语境：法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）　|　核心词汇：court　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 court 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 my uncle ① entered a court for the first time at the age of eleven times five, and he said the entering was the whole of the waiting. The ② court, meaning the room and not the judge, held eleven witnesses and stayed that full; court, he said, is the only thing in a building that is judged by how long people stand.

Every ③ court in that city had the same bench, and the ④ court at the end, meaning the one he kept for the appeal and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever returned to twice. Court, my aunt said, is nine parts bench and one part somebody willing to stand; my uncle said the standing is the part that fills the waiting.

My mother meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the court was the whole of the game, meaning the marked ground and not the room. The ⑥ court, meaning the marked ground and not any of that, is the only thing in a game that everybody runs on and nobody measures; court, she said, is either something you enter or the only word that means both a room and a marked ground. He said the marked ground is the part they remember.

By 1966 the ⑦ court had become a line in a summons, and the summons had become an argument about the bench. The ⑧ court of the whole thing, my uncle wrote in February, was one witness and thirty years of standing; court, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand. She said the standing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ court I remember is the one at the end, which he entered in 1972 and is still described as the fullest in the county. A ⑩ court, my aunt said in 1974, is the only thing that improves by being returned to; every court, she said, is a marked ground that has agreed to look like a room. She said the marked ground was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 法庭（指那间庭室本身，与那位法官相对）
C. 固定搭配：enter a court 走进法庭
D. n. 法院（指那座城市里每一个）
E. n. 法院（指末尾那一个）
F. n. 球场（指画好线的场地）
G. n. 法庭（指传票上提到的那一个）
H. n. 宫廷；朝廷（抽象总称，另一常见义）

items.q: entered a court for the first time at the age of eleven times five
The court, meaning the room and not the judge
the court was the whole of the game
The court, meaning the marked ground
the court had become a line in a summons
The court of the whole thing
A court, my aunt said in 1974

answers.why: enter a court 意为“走进法庭”，1958 年叔叔五十五岁时第一次走进法庭。
court 意为“法庭”，指那间庭室本身而不是那位法官，容纳了十一位证人。
court 指那座城市里每一个法院，每一个都摆着同样的长凳。
court 指末尾那一个（他留给上诉的那一个），是唯一有人回去过两次的。
court 意为“球场”，母亲说球场就是那场比赛的全部，指的是画好线的场地而不是那间庭室。
court 为体育用法，指画好线的场地而不是那间庭室，是比赛里人人在上面跑、却无人丈量的东西。
court 意为“法庭”，指传票上提到的那一个，到 1966 年这个法庭成了传票上的一行。
court 意为“宫廷、朝廷”，叔叔二月写道，整件事的朝堂是一位证人三十年的站立。
court 意为“法院、法庭”，我记得的是末尾那一个，他 1972 年走进去，至今仍被说成全县人最满的。
court 为抽象总称，姑姑说一个法庭是唯一会因为被回到而变好的东西。
